meta.title: Discover Altered — free trading card game
meta.description: A card game, free to play online, maintained by a community.
header.title: Discover Altered
toc.label: Contents
gameplay.lead: Each player leads a Hero and a Companion expedition, starting at opposite ends of a route built from Adventure cards. Play characters into an expedition, and at the end of the Day the stronger expedition moves forward. Bring your Hero and Companion together first and you win.
gameplay.diff.1.title: Packed with decisions, no downtime
gameplay.diff.1.body: You play a single card, then it is your opponent's turn. Take the initiative or hold back to react, thwart their plan or build your own: decisions come constantly and games stay short (20–40 minutes).
gameplay.diff.2.title: Nothing is decided until the end
gameplay.diff.2.body: Characters leave play at Night rather than piling up, so no one builds an unassailable lead. You can be behind in the race and still win it on the last Day.
gameplay.diff.3.title: When you play a card matters as much as which
gameplay.diff.3.body: Cards move to your Reserve at Night and can come back from there, possibly at a different cost and with different effects. Holding a card back, or spending it early to set up its return, changes what you can do in the coming Days.
gameplay.diff.4.title: Every card is also mana
gameplay.diff.4.body: Any card in hand can be placed as a Mana Orb. Every draw is a real choice, and no hand is ever dead.
gameplay.diff.5.title: Unique cards
gameplay.diff.5.body: Alongside the standard cards, Altered generates one-of-a-kind versions with their own abilities. No two collections look the same.
gameplay.diff.6.title: Easy to learn, hard to master
gameplay.diff.6.body: You will understand Altered in one game. It takes a lot longer to know which card to place as mana, anticipate what will be added to the Reserve before it overflows, and when to let a Day go.

gameplay.day.dawn.name: Morning
gameplay.day.dawn.text: Draw two, bury one as mana
gameplay.day.noon.name: Noon
gameplay.day.afternoon.name: Afternoon
gameplay.day.afternoon.text: One card each, until both pass
gameplay.day.dusk.name: Dusk
gameplay.day.night.name: Night
gameplay.visual.alt: The Altered board: two expeditions start at opposite ends of the route and move toward each other.
gameplay.cue.label: What happens in this Day
gameplay.cue.1: The top player plays Reka Fisherman from their hand into the Hero expedition.
gameplay.cue.2: The bottom player can't challenge the Hero expedition, so plays Kelon Elementary from their Reserve into the Companion expedition.
gameplay.cue.4: Each player advances in one expedition, and could not block the opponent in the other.
gameplay.cue.5: Night: the expeditions are cleared. Kelon Elementary was played from the Reserve, so it is discarded.
gameplay.cue.6: Reka Fisherman was played from the hand, so it goes to the Reserve for the next Days.
gameplay.visual.caption: Your Hero and your Companion start on either side of the Tumult. Bring them back together before your opponent does and the game is yours.
world.lead: A cataclysm called the Tumult reshaped the world and scattered the people who lived in it. We thought the world was lost; it had merely been transformed. Six factions have set out to rediscover it, and none of them is seeking the same thing.
world.chips.label: Factions
world.human: Every illustration in Altered is made by a human artist. We intend to keep it that way.
world.faction.ax.lore: No other Faction is as keen on innovation as the Axiom. For these machinists and engineers, researchers and inventors, the world is full of wonders and opportunities to be explored and harnessed. Its members are highly pragmatic: they firmly believe that through progress — whether technical, economic, or social — and the achievements of science, humanity will continue to improve its living conditions, so harshly tested by the Tumult.
world.faction.ax.play: The Axiom build. You lay down permanents turn after turn, you recycle whatever passes through your Reserve, and what looked like a laborious setup becomes a machine that no longer stops. This is the faction that wins late, provided it survives the first few Days: cut off its permanents or empty its Reserve, and the whole structure collapses. Pick it if you like placing pieces and watching them lock together.
world.faction.ax.name: Axiom
world.faction.br.lore: The philosophy of the Bravos is to confront the obstacles that litter their path, to meet the challenges that present themselves or that they impose on themselves in order to overcome them. They embrace danger, eagerly anticipating the opportunity to confront it and triumph. To be a Bravos is above all to break the status quo, to become better, to constantly push the limits: the boundaries and barriers that exist around them, but also their own limitations.
world.faction.br.play: The Bravos charge. Two ways to do it: cheap characters with high statistics, pushing both expeditions forward at once, or extra Mana Orbs to bring out giants well ahead of schedule. Either way you set the pace of the Day and your opponent follows it. The drawback is well known: your biggest cards are ideal targets for removal, and if the game drags on, you are the one who runs out of steam.
world.faction.br.name: Bravos
world.faction.ly.lore: When they contemplate the world, the Lyra understand how it is expression above all else. Every living being, every thing, exhales a cohort of ideas and emotions just by existing, like fragrances, like sensory explosions that must be felt to be truly understood and appreciated... Lyra Alterers rejoice in traversing such a cosmos, as vibrant as it is intense; to be pierced by its beauty, as moving as it is relentless.
world.faction.ly.play: The Lyra play with the rules. Dice rolls, characters specialised in one region type, cards that bend the shape of a Day: there is always a move your opponent did not expect, and rarely the one they were afraid of. In exchange you accept some randomness — the dice and the face-down Adventure cards can both turn on you — and you defend poorly. The faction for people who would rather surprise than control.
world.faction.ly.name: Lyra
world.faction.mu.lore: The Muna aspire to total alignment with their environment: a unity of mind, soul, and body that surpasses the prism of thought or reason. Only in this way can they embrace the flow of the world, becoming one with its currents... For members of the Faction, existence stems from the moment, and reality is a wave that must be ridden. For the Muna, the Tumult is a reflection of the living beings' disruption of harmony; a symptom, not a cause.
world.faction.mu.play: The Muna grow. You summon Plants, you anchor them so they stay for the following Days, then you make them bigger: after a few Days your opponent runs into a wall of statistics they can no longer cross. The plan is simple and readable, which makes this an excellent first faction. Its limit is there too: you barely interfere with your opponent, and one well-timed disruption cracks the whole structure.
world.faction.mu.name: Muna
world.faction.or.lore: The Ordis stands as a champion of order: for its members, everything must have its place and role; every being must be an essential link in a homogeneous and efficient whole, while flourishing in this function. Similarly, for the world to regain its stability and unity of old, it must once again be governed by immutable physical laws, without fearing the permanent inconsistency of the Tumult.
world.faction.or.play: The Ordis line things up. Where others look for the decisive card, you accumulate: recruits produced in series, characters whose passive effects quietly jam your opponent’s plan, and a position that solidifies Day after Day. Fast, by boosting your recruits, or slow, by stacking them up. A precise, almost surgical game, where a single point of statistics decides a Day, provided you accept the price.
world.faction.or.name: Ordis
world.faction.yz.lore: For the Yzmir mystics, the mind is the foundation of all things: it is the seat of ideas, and it is through it that they must be tamed. Like a blade that is sharpened, it must be honed to remain keen and penetrating. That is why the Yzmir Initiates practice meditation, develop philosophy, and spirituality. It is through them that their intellect and intuition will see beyond what the senses reveal, that their consciousness will pierce through the murky veils of reality.
world.faction.yz.play: The Yzmir answer. The best removal and draw spells in the game, characters that set the ground up for them, and synergies where you sacrifice your own to reach forbidden magic. You let your opponent commit first, then take their Day apart piece by piece. The price for that: a reactive plan is only worth anything if you are holding the right answer at the right moment. Anticipation is not optional here.
world.faction.yz.name: Yzmir
world.intro.name: The world
world.intro.1.title: The world
world.intro.1.body: Five centuries ago, the imaginary world collided with ours. The Confluence gave birth to the Tumult: currents that alter everything in their path, reshaping landscapes and creatures and leaving the world impossible to cross. The survivors wandered from Oasis to Oasis before gathering at Asgartha, a stabilised peninsula that became the last home of humanity.
world.intro.2.title: The reconquest
world.intro.2.body: Asgartha launched the Rediscovery Endeavor: pass beyond the walls, secure the lands one by one, and trace the Tumult back to its source to calm it. The Exalts are its vanguard, and every game of Altered is one of those expeditions. Six factions are leading that reconquest, each with its own idea of what humanity should become.
world.intro.3.title: The Exalts
world.intro.3.body: Alteration lets you give shape to your imagination by capturing Mana — the same energy that feeds the Tumult. Those who master it set out in pairs: an Alterer, who manifests their memories and ideas, and their Alter Ego, a Chimaera born of the Tumult able to capture far more of it. Bound together, they form an Exalt. That pair is what you play.
play.lead: Two ways to play, for free.
play.t1.title: Online, right now
play.t1.step1: Create a free Board Game Arena account.
play.t1.step2: Pick a faction and its ready-made starter deck.
play.t1.step3: Play the tutorial, then your first real game against a human.
play.t1.note: Board Game Arena applies the rules for you, so you can learn by playing.
play.t2.title: Around a table
play.t2.step1: Print proxies at home, or order printed cards from **Forgefire**, the officially approved service.
play.t2.step2: Find a game night near you, or a shop already running tables.
play.t2.step3: No one nearby? Start your own table. We give you the kit and the tournament tool.
play.t2.note: Printing cards for your own use is fine. Forgefire guarantees quality and quantity.
decks.lead: Starter decks are solid, and they teach you the game while you enjoy yourself. But there comes a point when you want to push your own idea further than they allow. That is where deckbuilding starts: a free account, every format, and a deck that looks like nobody else’s. Build it here and it is simply there in your next Board Game Arena game. No export, no file, no copying a list across.

decks.fmt.label: Formats
decks.fmt.closing: Tournaments always say which format they use.
decks.fmt.standard.name: Standard
decks.fmt.standard.what: The reference format: a deck of at least 39 cards led by one Hero, built from any card of any set, Unique cards included.
decks.fmt.standard.who: Everyone. It is the natural place to start, and the one to learn first.
decks.fmt.nuc.name: Standard, no uniques
decks.fmt.nuc.what: The Standard rules with one difference: no Unique cards. Every card in your deck is a regular card that anyone can own.
decks.fmt.nuc.who: Players who want a level field, or who have not collected Uniques.
decks.fmt.singleton.name: Singleton
decks.fmt.singleton.what: A bigger deck of at least 59 cards, with a single copy of each card. Unique cards are allowed.
decks.fmt.singleton.who: Deckbuilders who prefer variety to repetition: it plays very differently from Standard.
decks.fmt.singleton_nuc.name: Singleton, no uniques
decks.fmt.singleton_nuc.what: Singleton without Unique cards: a deck of at least 59 cards, one copy of each, all regular cards.
decks.fmt.singleton_nuc.who: Singleton players who want every card in the deck to be one anyone can own.
decks.fmt.frontier.name: Frontier
decks.fmt.frontier.what: The official Board Game Arena format. The deck-building rules are those of Standard, but Unique cards are only legal if they belong to a pool that is regularly changed, so the format keeps moving with the game.
decks.fmt.frontier.who: Competitive players, and anyone who likes digging through the Uniques to find the golden nuggets.
decks.fmt.frontier.unique: Allowed, from a pool that is regularly changed
decks.fmt.draft.name: Draft & Sealed
decks.fmt.draft.what: You open a pool of cards and build a deck from what you get. Nobody's collection matters, so a first-timer and a veteran start level.
decks.fmt.draft.who: Players who like freshness and creativity: every pool is different, so every deck is a new puzzle. It needs no collection at all.
project.lead.1: Equinox created Altered and carried it until March 2026, when the funding for its sixth set fell short. Before closing its services, the publisher released almost all of the cards, artwork and lore, and arranged the handover with Board Game Arena and the community.
project.lead.2: Since 20 May, the game has been in the hands of Altered Re:Union, a French non-profit association. Elected governance, published accounts, a team of volunteers around the world: development, rules, illustration, translation and tournaments are all handled by people who play the game.
